subject: Clarify DPA language & operational proof for LLM no-training and output rights
messages:
From: Claire Wu <claire.wu@acadiahealth.com>
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acadiahealth.com>, Acadia Legal <legal@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions re: no-training, outputs, and subprocessors

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the call earlier — Legal and Security asked me to capture a few outstanding items we need clarified before we sign the DPA and move forward with the pilot:

1) "No training" clause: Acadia wants an explicit commitment that tenant inputs and outputs will not be used to improve models (no re-training or fine-tuning) and that any internal model experiments are segregated. We also need operational attestations (logs, retention, KV cache expiration) to show how you implement the restriction.

2) Output ownership: we need confirmation that customer prompts + the generated responses are considered customer content and that Acadia retains rights to use/export derivatives. We want this reflected in the DPA/Terms.

3) Subprocessors & transfers: can you confirm your EU subprocessors and whether any model improvement vendors have access to raw prompts/responses (even aggregated)? Also advise on cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs? onshore KMS?).

4) Proof for procurement: a one‑page ops evidence matrix and a short sample redline for the DPA would help expedite Legal.

Can you send over the redline + a short operational note on how Redwood enforces the no-training promise?

Thanks,
Claire

--
Claire Wu
Director of Product Compliance, Acadia Health
claire.wu@acadiahealth.com

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acadiahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: no-training, outputs, and subprocessors

Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a first-pass redline and an ops evidence matrix (see attachments). Quick summary here so Legal has the high-level answers while we loop in Product + Ops:

- No-training commitment: Redwood will add the explicit no-training clause for Acadia tenant data. Operationally, we implement this by:
  * segregated processing paths for "no-learn" tenants (requests routed to a runtime that has training hooks disabled),
  * short-lived KV cache (configurable TTL, default 1 hour for this profile), and
  * strict telemetry filters — customer content is hashed at ingress and only used for anonymized metrics.

- Output / derivative rights: we propose language that grants Acadia ownership of prompts + generated responses for the term of the contract and allows export. We need to confirm whether you want us to license back aggregated, de-identified telemetry for product improvement; by default we exclude Acadia from any data used for model improvements.

- Subprocessors & transfers: attached is our current subprocessor snapshot and a note on transfer mechanisms. For onshore key control, we can support customer-managed KMS in the US and an SFTP export lane for periodic data pulls (SFTP + PGP).

I copied Jordan in case Legal has redline preferences. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your counsel tomorrow.

Best,
Michael

--
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

Attachments: Acadia_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx), ops_evidence_matrix.xlsx (xlsx), redline_summary.txt (txt)

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: DPA questions re: no-training, outputs, and subprocessors

Team — forwarding Acadia's ask. TL;DR: they want a contractual no‑training commitment + operational evidence and an export path. A few open items where I need your input:

Lauren — Legal wants tight wording on "ownership of outputs" vs. our standard licensing. They will likely push to state "Acadia retains all rights in prompts and outputs" and ask Redwood to remove any derivative license. Can we accept a clause that 1) gives Acadia ownership of prompts and responses and 2) disallows Redwood from using those materials for model training or improvement (explicitly) without opt‑in? If not, what's our acceptable middle ground?

Priyom — Ops: can you confirm the runtime config that enforces no-training for a tenant (routing to a no-learn fleet), KV cache TTL options, and KMS integration notes for customer-managed keys in us-east? Also need a short checklist we can include in the ops_evidence_matrix sheet (I flagged items for you).

We should keep tone pragmatic — Acadia is mid‑market but a reference in health; this is also an opportunity to bake an operational proof bundle we can reuse.

Thanks,
Michael

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: michael_grant@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 15:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: DPA questions re: no-training, outputs, and subprocessors

Michael / Priyom — quick notes:

1) Legal language: we can accept language that states "Customer retains all rights to customer prompts and responses; Redwood will not use such customer content to train models or to improve Redwood models without Customer's prior written consent." That is stronger than our default but acceptable for Health customers with the following clarifier: Redwood reserves the right to use aggregated, de-identified statistics derived from system telemetry that cannot be mapped back to Customer content. We should add an explicit definition of "de-identified" in the DPA redline to avoid ambiguity.

2) Ops controls (Priyom please confirm):
  - Routing: configure tenant flag no_learn=true which directs traffic to a dedicated runtime cluster with training hooks off.
  - KV cache: TTL configurable down to 5m; propose default 1h for this engagement. Documented in ops_evidence_matrix.
  - KMS: we can support customer-managed KMS in us-east-1 via an external key ARN — Ops will not have access to the key material.
  - Exports: SFTP + PGP support; we will populate the export with prompt+response bundles on customer schedule (weekly or ad hoc).
  - Audit logs: we can provide log slices showing routing and TTL enforcement for a rolling 90-day window.

3) Subprocessors: we will provide the current subprocessor list; commit that any vendor with access to plaintext customer content will be disclosed and require contractual non-training commitments. Note: some infra vendors in EU handle only orchestration (no access to content) — we must document their role clearly.

Priyom — can you produce the short ops checklist and a one‑page attestation that we can send to Acadia Legal? Michael, happy to join the call with Claire and their counsel tomorrow.

Lauren

--
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: michael_grant@redwood.ai
To: Claire Wu <claire.wu@acadiahealth.com>, Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@acadiahealth.com>, Acadia Legal <legal@acadiahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions re: no-training, outputs, and subprocessors

Claire / Jordan —

Thanks for the patience. Attaching the redline and an ops evidence matrix as discussed. Highlights:

- Contract: new clause proposed at Section 8.3 (redline attached) — "Customer retains all rights in customer inputs and outputs. Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or improve models without Customer's prior written consent." We included a definition of "de-identified" that requires irreversible pseudonymization and removal of unique identifiers.

- Ops evidence: the attached matrix lists concrete artifacts we will deliver upon request for the pilot (routing logs showing no_learn=true, KV cache TTL settings, KMS configuration verification, SFTP export samples, and SOC 2 subservice list).

- Subprocessors: current list included; we flagged the EU orchestration vendor (no plaintext access) and the US inference partner (has access to runtime logs only under strict ACLs). Any subprocessor with potential access to Customer Content will be contractually required to abide by the no-training restriction.

Next steps:
  1) Please review the attachments and let us know if Legal wants wording changes.
  2) If acceptable, we can circulate a DocuSign envelope for the DPA redline.
  3) Ops can provide an example export (SFTP/PGP) of a single day's prompt+response bundle for your review — confirm weekly vs. ad hoc.

Happy to jump on a call with Acadia Legal tomorrow morning (I am available 9–11 PT).

Best,
Michael

--
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
